questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three reasons this lesson gives for Python leading AI work?
options: A massive ecosystem of libraries like pandas, NumPy, and PyTorch
Every major AI provider ships its official SDK in Python first
Python has no competition from any other language in any domain
Readable syntax that puts less ceremony between an idea and working code
questions.explain: The lesson names readable syntax, ecosystem, and first-class AI support — not a blanket claim of no competition.

questions.q: What do PyTorch and TensorFlow have in common, according to this lesson?
options: They were both discontinued in favor of newer tools
They're the two frameworks behind nearly every modern AI model, and both are Python libraries at their core
Neither one supports Python at all
They are competing programming languages, not libraries
questions.explain: Both are Python libraries, and together they underlie most modern AI model training.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does most AI engineering work actually consist of?
options: Writing new programming languages for AI research
Manually labeling training data full time
Training large language models from scratch on massive datasets
Integration — calling a model's API, shaping data, handling responses, and wiring it into a real application
questions.explain: Training from scratch is a smaller, research-heavy specialty; most AI engineering work is integration.

questions.q: What does this course assume about your prior programming experience?
options: Fluency in a different language like Java or C++
Nothing — zero prior programming is assumed
At least one year of professional software development
Completion of a separate statistics course first
questions.explain: The course is the entry point of the AI Engineer path and assumes no prior programming at all.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say each topic in the course was chosen?
options: Because it is required for a specific certification exam
Because it is the easiest material to generate automatically
Because every other programming course covers the same topics in the same order
Because it shows up directly in real AI-engineering code, not because it's a classic computer-science topic
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that topics earn their place by appearing in real AI-engineering work.
